Seminar Title:

Numerical Investigation of Hemodynamic Responses in Intracranial Aneurysms under Hypertensive Conditions

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Mechanical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Gaurav Kumar ( Rollno : 519me1022)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Room number ME-001, Department of Mechanical Engineering (Hybrid mode)

Date and Time:

11 Sep 2026 11 AM

Contact:

Sumit Kumar

Abstract:

Intracranial aneurysms (IAs) are life-threatening cerebrovascular disorders whose rupture risk is closely linked to local hemodynamic forces. Changes in the hemodynamic parameters lead to the degradation of the endothelial layer. Thus, understanding the hemodynamics of the aneurysm is necessary with more realistic boundary conditions. The increasing case of hypertension and its severity also leads to the exploration of the hypertension and hypotension on the aneurysm hemodynamics.

This work aims to predict the hemodynamics in unruptured IAs and investigate the impact of aneurysm necking and bulging, along with hypotension and hypertension, on the same. Aneurysm necking and bulging significantly alter flow patterns, correlating geometry with unique vortex modes and maximum WSS. The developed flow regime map aids in diagnosing and treating aneurysms under varying conditions. High pulsatility indices, particularly in younger individuals, amplify risks, highlighting the need for tailored management strategies.

This study presents a detailed numerical investigation of IAs treated with shape memory polymer (SMP) foam and coil embolization. The embolized regions are modeled as porous media, with permeability and form factor values derived from existing literature for SMP foam and two coil configurations. A validated solver, incorporating a non-Newtonian Quemada viscosity model and inlet conditions, is used to capture transient hemodynamics. Velocity fields, vortex structures, WSS, and relative residence time (RRT) are analyzed to understand the effect of embolization. SMP foam significantly reduces intra-aneurysmal velocity and WSS while enhancing RRT, indicating a higher potential for stable thrombus formation compared to coils. Hypertension increases intra-aneurysmal flow and WSS, which may compromise treatment success, while hypotension enhances flow stagnation and increases RRT. The results demonstrate that SMP foam embolization offers superior flow disruption and clot-promoting conditions. It is also noted that inducing mild hypotension during or post-treatment may support improved clinical outcomes from a hemodynamics perspective.
